newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 falls to end week 2.6 percent lower.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 falls to end week 2.6 percent lower.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange's PX50 index continued to fall on Friday on profit-taking which analysts expect will level off next week.
The index fell 4.4. points, or 0.72 percent, on Friday to 609.2, closing the week 2.61 percent lower despite posting a two-year high on Tuesday of 629.0 points.
Major banking issues Komercni Banka a.s., Ceska Sporitelna a.s. and IPB a.s. all fell, and small gains to the market's biggest share, SPT Telecom a.s., failed to offset the losses.
Komercni lost 55 crowns to close at 2,750 before it announced that its net 1996 profit, according to international accounting standards, rose to 5,24 billion crowns from 5.11 in 1995.
Analysts said the results were dissapointing, as last year's rising interest rates should have given way to stronger profit figures.
Overall on the market, losers led gainers by 277 to 227, while 155 issues remained unchanged. A total of 1.65 million shares changed hands on modest turnover of 1.86 billion crowns.
